judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-2.1 (representing numbers by place value, reading number names) and Curricular Goal CG-2. The first (Class-3, rank 2) covers visualising and estimating numbers up to 999 (LCs: 'Visualise numbers up to 999', 'Estimate numbers up to 999'); the second (Class-4, rank 3) extends the same number-sense strand to numbers and number names up to 10000 grounded in place value (LCs: 'Represent numbers up to 10000 based on place value', 'Read number names up to 10000'). judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class-5 (rank 4) Content statements under the same measurement Curricular Goal CG-4 ('measure attributes such as distance, length, weight, area, capacity and time ... relating measure and number'), but sit under different competencies: C-4.3 (unit conversion within a measurement system, applied to everyday problems) and C-4.4 (strategies to estimate time). Their LCs show genuine skill coherence rather than mere wording overlap: 'convert units of length among metres, centimetres and millimetres' / 'convert units of weight among kilograms, grams and milligrams' alongside 'convert time between the 12-hour clock and the 24-hour clock' — the shared 'conversion' idea of re-expressing one measured quantity in an alternative unit/notation, reinforcing measurement sense across attributes. However, metric length/mass conversion is decimal and multiplicative while 12/24-hour clock conversion is a base-60/notation reading convention, so neither is evidenced as supporting success in the other; at equal Class-5 rank there is no substantive evidence for a developmental direction. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context and truncated source evidence (33 and 24 omitted items), so unseen source detail could refine but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under CG-2 (whole-number fluency). Direction follows the resolved Class-3 -> Class-4 coordinates; confidence is moderate because the target text is a terse bullet and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content SFIs about arranging/ordering: Class-1 'Reorders quantities by number' (under Competency C 1.5 'Learns to order and arrange, developing intuition of number') and Class-2 '• Arranging pictures' (under Competency C-1.13 'Develops computational thinking through problem solving strategies', LC 'Arrange pictures in a logical order'). They share a genuine ordering/sequencing skill family and reinforce each other across representations (numerical quantity vs. pictorial sequence), which supports substantive conceptual coherence. However, the Class-2 item sits in a distinct computational-thinking/sequencing competency rather than number sense, and the only LC token shared is 'ordering' (jaccard 0.14); ordering by numerical magnitude is not evidenced as a supporting proficiency for logically sequencing pictures, so a developmental first_to_second buildsTowards is not warranted despite the Class-1 to Class-2 rank gap. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (34 and 24 omitted items), so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts, LC text, and ancestor competency statements.

judgment.rationale: Both Content SFIs sit under Competency C-4.2 (selecting suitable units and tools for measurement) within CG-4 and address weight measurement with a balance, but they differ substantively in demand. The Class-3 item (rank 2) is 'Weight: kilogram, more than/ less than 1 kilogram, using simple balance', with LCs about comparing objects as heavier/lighter than 1 kg and measuring in kilograms with a simple balance. The Class-4 item (rank 3) is 'Measuring weight of the objects (gram) using weighing balance', with an LC on measuring weight in grams. This is lower-to-higher rank movement from coarse comparison against a single kilogram benchmark to quantified measurement in the finer standard unit (gram) on a weighing balance; competence with balance use and the kilogram benchmark supports success with gram-level measurement. Shared wording and page/rank proximity alone were not treated as sufficient; the unit and precision shift provides the pair-specific developmental justification. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, but the retained statement and LC text is unambiguous.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 Content bullets under CG-2 (fluency with whole numbers, place value and simple fractions and their comparison), but under different competencies: the first sits under C-2.2 (represents and compares commonly used fractions as parts of a whole/points on a number line) with LC 'compare fractions using activity and material rather than as an algorithm'; the second sits under C-2.1 (place-value representation and comparison of numbers) with LCs 'compare/order/sequence numbers beyond 10000'. The substantive coherence is the shared comparison-of-magnitude reasoning applied to two different number domains (whole numbers vs. concrete fraction models), which is complementary reinforcement rather than one being a deepening or extension of the other. Both endpoints share the same resolved coordinate rank (Class-5, rank 4) and the evidence contains no substantive same-rank signal establishing that proficiency in one supports success in the other, so no buildsTowards direction is asserted; nomination signals were weak (single shared token 'compare'/'comparing', weak page and rank proximity). Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded text and LCs shown.
